_about: What Saudi students actually type, and what our page must carry to be the answer. Sources: Google (hl=ar, gl=sa) and Bing (mkt=ar-SA) autocomplete pulled live on 2026-10-31 (213 seeds, 1,871 suggestions; tools/seo/suggest.js re-runs it), and ten answer-engine probes the same day, in which every reply opened with the formula as text, then one worked example, then the trap. tools/seo/audit.js checks each query automatically: is there an indexable page whose text carries `expect` (a rule's formula from js/data, or its teaching-card wording, plus any `text`) and, when `titleHas` is set, whose <title> contains one of those words. Checking the engines themselves is by hand: ask each query in each engine in `engines`, then add a row to `log` with what you saw. Record only what you saw; never estimate a position or a citation. `page` names the page we mean to answer a query; the audit warns when that page does not carry the answer. A query about one rule (`expect.rule`) is meant for that rule's lesson page, and its `page` says so; the audit warns when `page` is another page (unless `pageWhy` says why) and when another of our pages would answer the query better than the one meant for it.
